sessionLengthRationale: A short product default, not a scientifically established optimum.
onboarding: Ask target language and preferred variety.
Offer optional native language for explanations; do not infer ability from nationality.
Check playback and demonstrate A, B and X using audio only. Explain which sound, feature, tone or stress pattern to compare.
Explain that X is a different word and that the answer concerns its target category, not the whole word.

adaptation.basis: Per-contrast first-attempt ABX performance, tracked separately by word/voice familiarity, audio-only versus text-assisted trials, phoneme versus feature task, and voice condition.
adaptation.errorAction: Give contrastive feedback, then revisit after intervening trials with a different reviewed token when available.
adaptation.intervalStatus: Heuristic starting schedule; adjust against delayed performance.

separateModes: trained words vs genuinely held-out words
trained voices vs genuinely held-out voices
measurement.provisionalProgressRule: Only consider a contrast reliable after repeated first-attempt success across days, multiple word pairs, and an available held-out check. Display the evidence count and test type.
measurement.insufficientInventory: With only two pairs per contrast or trial group, cross-word practice is possible but there is no untouched-word transfer test after both pairs have been heard. Do not call a different word in the current trial a held-out word.

avoid: public rankings presented as language ability

audioReleaseGate: License permits commercial use, redistribution and caching for this asset.
Recording says the intended word with the declared dialect and contrast.
No incorrect stress, tone, dropped segment or generated extra word.
No filename, speaker selection, silence pattern or loudness cue reveals the answer.
Source type is accurately labeled; synthetic voices are not called human recordings.
Audio playback is checked on actual target browsers and mobile devices.
Every ABX category has correctly pronounced clips for the selected voices; A/B/X never expose the target text through pre-answer UI or accessibility labels.

abx.instruction: Listen to A, B, then X. Which reference shares X’s target sound?
abx.specialInstructions: Use target feature, tone or stress pattern instead of target sound when contrast.abx.matchType requires it.
abx.referencePair: Use the two words in one curated pair. Randomly assign category 0/1 to display roles A/B.
abx.targetX: Choose a different pair in the same contrast and the same abx.trialGroup. Pick the word with the desired category index; reject either reference word text.
abx.correctAnswer: The A/B display role whose category index equals X’s category index. Never infer from word spelling, array display position or voice.
abx.eligibility: Each reference pair needs at least one other pair with eligible words in its trial group. If none exists, show content unavailable; never silently substitute identical-clip matching.
abx.referenceVoices: Prefer one reviewed voice for both A and B, with X from a different reviewed voice. Both voices must cover both categories.
abx.singleVoiceFallback: A different word for X still prevents exact-waveform matching. Label this within-voice practice, vary independently recorded tokens when available, and keep its results separate.
abx.threeVoiceOption: With sufficient reviewed voices, A/B/X may use distinct voices; randomize assignments independently of answer and track the condition.
abx.audioSequence: Play full reviewed words in A-B-X order with consistent spacing; allow individual replays. A 500 ms gap is a testable starting choice, not a universally optimal interval.
abx.textVisibility: Hide words, IPA, pinyin, meanings, category labels that expose spelling, word-bearing filenames and accessibility labels until the first answer or explicit text-assist opt-in.
abx.audioOnlyLabels: Playback and response controls say A, B or X. A neutral target-location instruction may be visible. Text guides remain separate reading material.
abx.textAssistMeasurement: If a learner enables text before answering, mark the trial text-assisted and exclude it from audio-only accuracy.
abx.feedback: After the first answer, identify the matching A/B category, allow A/B/X replay and optionally reveal words, IPA and meanings. Explain the target category without treating X as the same whole word.
abx.researchLimit: ABX is the chosen product task. Categorical discrimination has research support, but neither ABX superiority nor this specific cross-word app algorithm has been established.
